ap_exam_scope_notes.note: Mass spectra involving nonsingly charged monatomic species or complex sample mixtures are not assessed as required spectrum interpretations.
Assignment of four quantum numbers to individual electrons is outside assessed scope.
Writing configurations for elements that are exceptions to the Aufbau principle is not assessed.
Derivation or depiction of hybrid orbitals, hybridization involving d orbitals, and molecular orbital diagrams are not assessed.
Phase-diagram interpretation is outside the assessed scope.
Colligative properties and calculations of solution molality or solution percent-by-mass/volume are outside scope.
Rote memorization of solubility rules beyond the College Board specified simple cases is not assessed; terminology of oxidizing/reducing agents is excluded.
Lewis acid–base theory is excluded; use Brønsted–Lowry concepts.
Numerical Arrhenius equation calculations are excluded.
Converting between Kc and Kp is not assessed.
Numerical concentrations of each species along polyprotic titration curves are excluded; qualitative speciation remains relevant.
Calculations of salt solubility as a function of pH are excluded; qualitative trends are relevant.
Assigning positive/negative labels to electrodes is not assessed; anode/cathode and directions remain relevant.
Focus on qualitative meaning of the Nernst equation and concentration effects; numerical substitution alone is insufficient evidence of understanding.

common_misconception_candidates.label: Counts a double bond as two electron domains
Assigns hydrogen bonding without identifying a suitably bonded H donor
Confuses intermolecular attraction with a covalent bond within one molecule
Answers molecular geometry when hybridization is requested, or vice versa
Treats molar mass as the full explanation of dispersion forces without electron-cloud polarizability
Explains boiling as breaking intramolecular covalent bonds
